title: Emrys and the Alibi
premise: Insurance investigator Lena Whitlock receives two letters about the unsolved Harrowgate fire that killed her father twenty years ago: one confessing to arson, one promising a second confession if she can find its sender before the anniversary. Using her photographic memory of the original case file, Lena discovers the letters quote details never made public, meaning the writer had access to sealed evidence—likely someone inside the investigation itself. As she closes in, she realizes the confessor is dying and wants justice done outside the law's reach, while a second party is killing everyone who could corroborate the truth. In the end, Lena must choose between exposing the killer through legal channels or honoring the dying man's wish, and she chooses a third path: publishing the truth herself, inheriting not her father's estate but his unfinished fight.
about_author: Lior Underhill is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters for a living. They write mysteries from a converted fire station in coastal Maine, where the alarm bell still works.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Lena Whitlock's POV. On an ordinary Tuesday, two envelopes arrive: one confessing to the Harrowgate fire, one unsigned, promising 'the rest' if Lena finds its author within thirty days. The confession quotes file numbers from evidence sealed when Lena was nine years old. Emotional beat: the cold professional's carefully ordered life cracks open as memory floods back unbidden.

chapters.title: The File That Remembers Me
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She pulls her photographic recall of the 2004 case file and finds the letters match details redacted even from investigators—a burn pattern, a shifted gas valve. Her old mentor, Detective Sorrel, deflects her questions and warns her off. Emotional beat: unease deepening into resolve; the past isn't closed, it's curated.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Lena visits the rebuilt Harrowgate property, now owned by the Ashcombe Trust, and interviews the caretaker, Mr. Pell, whose answers are rehearsed. She notices fresh paint over a scorch mark in the cellar. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into investigative hunger; the house remembers what people won't say.

chapters.title: A Witness, Briefly
chapters.summary: Lena tracks down retired firefighter Dana Okafor, first on scene in 2004. Dana confirms the gas valve anomaly but refuses to go on record. Two days later, Dana dies in a single-car accident. Emotional beat: dread—the letters weren't an invitation, they were a countdown, and someone is erasing the past faster than Lena can read it.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following the unsigned letter's riddle—a line from her father's insurance ledger—she finds a second letter hidden in a bank deposit box: the writer admits to being inside the investigation, claims the fire was set to destroy documents implicating the Ashcombe Trust, and says he is dying. Emotional beat: vertigo; justice may require trusting a confessed criminal.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Silence
chapters.summary: Lena confronts Sorrel with the second letter. He admits he was pressured to close the case in 2004 but denies writing the letters—and produces proof: he received an identical letter himself. Someone is playing them against each other. Emotional beat: betrayal and reluctant alliance; two keepers of the same wound finally compare scars.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Lena and the confessor, revealed as former forensic accountant Elias Vann, hiding in a hospice under a false name. Through his chapters we learn he copied the trust's ledgers before the fire and has been waiting, terminally ill, for someone incorruptible to find him. Emotional beat: tragic patience; a man spending his last weeks curating his own reckoning.

chapters.title: Ashcombe's Hand
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The trust's director, Marguerite Ashcombe, invites Lena to tea and offers her a settlement and silence, revealing she knows about Vann. Leaving, Lena realizes Marguerite's assistant was the anonymous second correspondent—protecting Vann from the trust's cleaner, who killed Okafor. Emotional beat: fury sharpened into strategy; the enemy has shown its face.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Trap
chapters.summary: Climax. On the fire's twentieth anniversary, Lena stages a public reading of Vann's ledger at the Harrowgate property, forcing the cleaner to act in front of witnesses while Sorrel records everything. The cleaner is caught; Marguerite, implicated by the ledger, is arrested. Vann dies peacefully hours later. Emotional beat: catharsis through exposure—truth as a trap sprung in daylight.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Resolution, Lena's POV. Weeks later, a final envelope arrives: Vann's will leaves Lena the complete ledgers and his testimony recordings, naming her executor of a justice the courts only partially delivered. She publishes the full account, closing her father's case in the open rather than in a file. Emotional beat: quiet peace; some inheritances aren't money—they're unfinished work, now hers to finish.
